Touching any other file fails the check.

## What was measured

On 2026-08-11 the candidate feeder was run live, with real credentials injected exactly as the scheduled runner injects them. Three channels came back reached: gmail, linkedin, bee. HubSpot came back UNREACHED with the detail "HubSpot credentials were unavailable" — while a valid API key was sitting in its environment.

The reason is in build_client(). It calls _credentials(), which returns a pair, and then refuses unless BOTH the API key and HUBSPOT_PORTAL_ID are non-empty. The portal id is then handed to _HubSpotClient, stored on the instance, and never read again — the request headers authenticate with the bearer token alone, which is how HubSpot v3 works. Nothing anywhere in this repository sets HUBSPOT_PORTAL_ID, and no secret reference supplies one.

So the channel declines to try, every run, and reports the same thing it would report if it had tried and failed.

HubSpot is a SECOND-ORDER source: it cannot establish a touch and its coverage does not gate a cold open. What it can do is corroborate a touch that was logged directly in the CRM rather than sent by email, which is the entire reason the second-order tier exists. Right now the loop never gets that.

## What to change

Make the portal id optional. A bearer token is sufficient to attempt a read:

  * build_client() returns a client when HUBSPOT_API_KEY is available, whether or not a portal id is.
  * build_client() still returns None — never raises — when there is no API key at all. A client that cannot authenticate must not be presented as a readable channel; that would turn a failed read into an empty inbox, which is the failure this whole subsystem exists to prevent.
  * If a portal id IS present, keep passing it through. Do not delete the plumbing, just stop requiring it.
  * Keep _credentials() reading from the environment first and the operator's file second, exactly as now.

Change nothing else. Do not touch observe(), map_records(), fetch(), or the record shape. Do not add a dependency. This is a small, surgical diff.

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u18_hubspot_reachable_check.py --worktree "$PWD"
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/contact_source_check.py --worktree "$PWD" --source hubspot --owned server/pipeline/contact_sources/hubspot_source.py

The first is the new behaviour; the second is the unchanged adapter contract, which must not regress. Note that the first check points HOME at a directory that does not exist, so the operator's file cannot influence the result — do not try to satisfy it by reading a file.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of BOTH check commands. Under 'Risk' say what happens if HubSpot returns an authentication error at run time now that the channel will actually attempt a read. Under 400 words.
